title: Current Affairs & Schemes
intro: Current affairs is the one GA area that ages, so this chapter deliberately concentrates on the durable backbone — the names and launch years of major government schemes, the headquarters of important organisations, recurring sporting events, and the international groupings SSC asks about. Pair this stable core with a habit of monthly current-affairs reading for the latest names and events.

topics.name: Government Schemes
topics.details: Know each flagship scheme by its purpose and launch year (these don't change). The objective and the year are the usual question.

solved.problem: In which year was the Swachh Bharat Mission launched?
Which scheme provides free LPG connections to poor households?
Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) is associated with which sector?
solved.solution: Health insurance (up to ₹5 lakh per family per year).

solved.problem: What is the aim of the Jan Dhan Yojana?
solved.solution: Financial inclusion — a bank account for every household.

unsolved.problem: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched in which year?
Which scheme promotes domestic manufacturing?
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana relates to?
Ujjwala Yojana provides free ___ connections.
Digital India was launched in?

topics.name: Organisations & Headquarters
topics.details: Organisation headquarters are stable, high-frequency facts. Pair each body with its city.

solved.problem: Where is the headquarters of the WHO?
Where is the headquarters of ISRO?
Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
Where is the SAARC secretariat located?

unsolved.problem: UNESCO is headquartered in?
The IMF and World Bank are headquartered in?
The RBI is headquartered in?
OPEC has its headquarters in?
Interpol is headquartered in?

topics.name: Sports & Events
topics.details: Recurring sporting events and their cycles are durable facts. Specific recent winners change — check a current-affairs source for the latest.

solved.problem: How often are the Summer Olympic Games held?
The Ranji Trophy is associated with which sport?
The FIFA World Cup is held once every how many years?
The Asian Games are held every how many years?

unsolved.problem: The ICC Cricket World Cup (ODI) is held roughly every ___ years.
The Ranji Trophy belongs to which sport?
The Commonwealth Games are held every ___ years.
The FIFA World Cup is the top event in which sport?
The Summer Olympics happen once every ___ years.

topics.name: Appointments & Summits
topics.details: SSC asks about the official ROLE behind an appointment and about recurring international groupings — facts that stay valid. For the latest office-holders and summit hosts, rely on monthly current-affairs updates.

solved.solution: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa.

solved.problem: Which grouping consists of India, the US, Japan and Australia?
G20 is a group of how many major economies?
SAARC is a regional grouping of which region?

unsolved.problem: The "C" in BRICS stands for?
ASEAN is a grouping of which region?
The QUAD includes India, USA, Japan and ___.
G20 comprises how many economies?
BRICS includes which two of the largest countries by area/population?

shortcuts: Learn each scheme with its launch year and one-line purpose.
Many flagship schemes launched in 2014–2015 (Swachh Bharat, Jan Dhan, Make in India, Digital India).
Pair every organisation with its HQ city (WHO–Geneva, UN–New York, ISRO–Bengaluru).
Memorise grouping members: BRICS, QUAD, G20, SAARC, ASEAN.
For names that change (office-holders, latest winners), read a monthly current-affairs digest.
mistakes: Placing an organisation's HQ in the wrong city (Interpol is Lyon, not Paris).
Memorising volatile names instead of durable roles/groupings.
Confusing BRICS members with G20 or QUAD members.
pyq: SSC asks scheme purpose/year, organisation HQs, event cycles and grouping membership — the durable core here — plus a few items from the last 6–12 months. Master the stable facts, then top up with recent affairs.

flashcards.a: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa

summary: Anchor current affairs to its durable backbone: flagship schemes with their launch years and purposes, organisation headquarters, event cycles, and international groupings (BRICS, QUAD, G20). These never go stale; layer the latest names and events on top with regular monthly reading.
